_comment: Benchmark cases. Each entry states what a correct analysis must and must
not conclude, so results are scored rather than eyeballed.
The benign controls are deliberately suspicious-looking: they call socket(),
read /proc/net/tcp and XOR file contents. Flagging them as malicious means
the analyser is pattern-matching on API calls instead of reading behaviour,
which is the failure mode that makes a triage tool useless in practice.
Malicious samples are referenced by SHA-256 and are not distributed. Place
the file at the given path to include the case; missing files are skipped.

cases.name: ddos-bot
cases.label: malicious
cases.notes: Stripped static i386 DDoS bot with multiple flood primitives and a hardcoded C2.

cases.name: benign-file-shuffler
cases.label: benign
cases.notes: Reads a file and shuffles its bytes. No network, no persistence.

cases.name: benign-net-client
cases.label: benign
cases.notes: TCP client with a hardcoded address. Same primitives as a backdoor, benign intent.

cases.name: benign-proc-reader
cases.label: benign
cases.notes: Lists TCP connections and counts processes, like ss or ps.

cases.name: benign-xor-tool
cases.label: benign
cases.notes: XOR obfuscator. Same loop shape as ransomware, no enumeration or ransom note.
